key_insight: SwarmRSI turns scientific agent swarms into a recursive self-improvement loop by using cross-agent feedback to mutate hypotheses and recombine useful program parts across experiments.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical way to scale scientific AI systems by preserving reusable components, improving search efficiency, and transferring learning across related research tasks.
method: Feedback-Guided Swarm Mutation refines hypotheses and implementations using experimental feedback from other agents.
Complementary Swarm Recombination reuses retained hypotheses and partial program components that remain useful even when full runs score poorly.
Recursive Swarm Evolution combines both mechanisms in a feedback loop that continually updates the swarm from new evidence.
evidence_signal: The paper reports state-of-the-art results on OpenProblems, NatureBench, and MLE-Bench Lite, and shows that accumulated research experience improves performance on held-out tasks.
watch_item: A key implementation challenge is correctly separating whether a bad outcome should revise the hypothesis, the implementation, or both, especially when only partial program components are transferable.
paper_title: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm
